dropped: the f=1 case (S_0, T_0 identities, B empty, only the final two-bit XOR runs)
items.note: The page puts the whole lemma together: eight-step parity gadget, packed cyclic shifts, guard set B, union bound, correction by extraction/radix sort/reinsertion, cost totals and the asymptotic simplification. Its order and its argument match the paper's proof.

The page uses translation invariance ('tests see only parities, so a=b=0 suffices') and works one substitution explicitly ('(0,0)->(-1,0)->(-1,0)->(0,0)->(0,1)'), which is correct. It then says 'likewise' for the rest of (00 01 10) and for (01 10 11). The method is the paper's, but only one of the substitutions is shown.
The composition is listed corner by corner ('00->01->10, 01->10->11, 10->00, 11->01'), giving (00 10)(01 11). This is correct.

dropped: the c=0 case (all eight operations do nothing) is not stated; only c=1 is analysed
items.note: From 'the product (00 10)(01 11) moves corners horizontally' the page reads off u'=u+c(1-2(u mod 2)), w'=w, with floor halves preserved. It gives the paper's sharper displacement bound, 'four unit steps move each coordinate at most four', which suffices for the eight used later.

dropped: explicit disjointness of the f-1 segments, the highest ending immediately below j_{f-1}
items.note: The setup u_i=2g_i+a_i (a_i=y_{j_i}), w_i=2h_i+b_i in z, g_i<2^{K-1}, c_i=x_{j_i}, i<f-1 is given correctly. The page also says position j_{f-1} is handled separately in O(V).

The page gives the shift formula with sign epsilon and parity beta, and the bijection reason ('whose offset ignores y, so it is a bijection, as are lines updating z'), as in the paper. It leaves implicit that 2^{j_i} is a unit step of segment i and that z_{j_i} is the parity of w_i.

dropped: bits below j_0 and above the highest used segment are untouched
items.note: 'Elsewhere segments start in [20,2^K-21], so moves <=8 never carry between segments and S_0=T_0'. The interval follows correctly from the guard interval [10,2^{K-1}-11], and the no-carry argument is the paper's.

dropped: K>=6, needed so that the twenty excluded values are distinct (2^{K-1}>=20)
items.note: 'Each guard excludes twenty of 2^{K-1} values, all equally frequent, so a union bound over 2(f-1) guards gives |B|<=delta M'. Here 20*2(f-1)/2^{K-1}=80(f-1)2^{-K}, and 'for any records' matches the paper's independence from record values.
The paper's argument is reproduced: 'T_0 keeps guards, so T_0(B)=B', and the two maps are bijections agreeing on B^c, so S_0(B)=B. Hence T_0S_0^{-1} fixes B^c and permutes B.

dropped: the offset is computed from the two controls alone in L^{O(1)} time and absorbed by the 2^L target blocks per fiber, which is what makes the rotation O(V)
items.note: Each rotation is a swap 'behind its controls and back' at O(VL^tau) plus a controlled cyclic shift at O(V), and the page cites at most sixteen swaps and eight rotations. The mechanism is the paper's, but the cost of computing the offsets is not addressed.

dropped: keys are distinct (because T_0S_0^{-1} permutes B)

items.note: 'Extracting B's records keyed by destination rank, radix-sorting them, and reinserting them in one scan gives T_0, as keys equal the vacated ranks.' This is correct and follows from the previous paragraph, but it is terse.

items.note: The three cost terms O(V(L^tau+1)), O(MA^3+V) and O(|B|A(R+A)) match the paper. The movement term follows from the swap and rotation counts above, but the per-record O(A^3) is asserted without justification.

The page divides by V to get A^3/R and 80(f-1)2^{-K}A(1+A/R), then lists the family hypotheses (A=O(p), R/p^C->infinity, f<=p, K/log p->infinity) under which both are o(1). This is correct and matches the paper.

items.note: 'a fixed invertible binary m x m matrix and its inverse, each a fixed number of packed row additions, cost O(V((eK)^tau+1))', with L=(e/m)K<=eK. This follows from the lemma's bound and matches the paper.

errors.problem: A_rect=ceil(log_2(2V)) is not the length of the rank. The paper pads destination ranks to ceil(log_2 M) <= A_rect bits and uses A_rect as a bound on the bit length of every integer involved, records and keys included.
